newsitem.title: USA: Columbia/HCA sued by two more pensions- WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Columbia/HCA sued by two more pensions- WSJ.

text.p: Two more big pension funds have filed lawsuits against Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp., the Wall Street Journal said on Tuesday.

The newspaper said in its electronic edition that the Florida State Board of Administration and the Louisiana Teachers Retirement System filed separate lawsuits aginst the company late last week, seeking damages from Columbia and some of its directors, the paper said.
The lawsuits were similar to the one filed by New York State Comptroller H. Carl McCall, the newspaper said.
Meanwhile, Columbia said two more executive are leaving the company.
Samuel Greco, senior vice president for financial operations, and Stephen Braun, the company general counsel, will resign, the newspaper said.
Neither has set a date for their departures, the paper said. Last month federal prosecutors confirmed that Columbia is the target of a federal probe into possible Medicare fraud.
